record.paper_title: Open questions concerning Weiszfeld's algorithm for the Fermat-Weber location problem
record.original_question: For the Fermat-Weber location problem, where one seeks a point in R^n minimizing the weighted sum of Euclidean distances to m given points in R^n, consider Weiszfeld's iterative algorithm in the noncollinear setting discussed for Kuhn's convergence claim. If the algorithm is initialized at a point in the affine subspace spanned by the m given points, does the sequence of iterates converge to the unique optimal solution for all but a denumerable set of starting points in that affine subspace?

evidence.quote: We then conjecture that if this algorithm is initiated at the affine subspace spanned by the m given points, the convergence is ensured

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $a_1,\dots,a_m \in \mathbb{R}^n$ be $m\ge 2$ distinct points (the "given points") that are not all collinear, and let $w_1,\dots,w_m>0$ be positive weights. The Fermat–Weber location problem is to find $x\in\mathbb{R}^n$ minimizing
$$F(x)=\sum_{i=1}^{m} w_i\, \|x-a_i\|_2.$$
Under the noncollinearity assumption $F$ is strictly convex on $\mathbb{R}^n$ and admits a unique minimizer $x^\ast$.

Weiszfeld's iteration is defined, for any current iterate $x^k\notin\{a_1,\dots,a_m\}$, by
$$x^{k+1} = T(x^k) := \left(\sum_{i=1}^{m}\frac{w_i}{\|x^k-a_i\|_2}\right)^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^{m}\frac{w_i\, a_i}{\|x^k-a_i\|_2}.$$
The iteration is undefined (and stopped) at any iterate equal to one of the $a_i$.

Let $A\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n$ be the affine hull of $\{a_1,\dots,a_m\}$. Prove or disprove: the set
$$B = \{x^0\in A : \text{the Weiszfeld sequence } (x^k)_{k\ge 0} \text{ starting at } x^0 \text{ either reaches some } a_i \text{ in finitely many steps or fails to converge to } x^\ast\}$$
is at most countable (denumerable). Equivalently, for all but countably many starting points in the affine subspace spanned by the given points, the Weiszfeld iteration converges to the unique optimal solution $x^\ast$.
artifact.status_search_result: The conjecture, attributed to Chandrasekaran and Tamir (1989), was proved by J. Brimberg. An earlier 1995 proof attempt was challenged by counterexamples of Cánovas, Marín and Cañavate (2002), but Brimberg's 2003 paper "Further notes on convergence of the Weiszfeld algorithm" (and the related "The Fermat–Weber location problem revisited") modifies the argument and establishes that, when the convex hull of the given points is full-dimensional (in particular within the affine hull of the points), the set of starting points from which Weiszfeld's iteration fails to converge to the optimum is at most countable. The conjecture is therefore considered settled in the affirmative.

status_evidence.title: Further notes on convergence of the Weiszfeld algorithm (Brimberg, 2003)
status_evidence.snippet: Brimberg modifies the earlier proof in light of counterexamples by Cánovas, Marín and Cañavate, and re-establishes the Chandrasekaran–Tamir conjecture that the set of bad starting points in the affine hull is denumerable.
status_evidence.claim: The Chandrasekaran–Tamir conjecture is proved (re-closed) in this 2003 paper.

status_evidence.title: The Fermat–Weber location problem revisited (Brimberg)
status_evidence.snippet: Provides a proof that the set of starting points for which Weiszfeld's algorithm fails to converge to the unique optimum is denumerable when the convex hull of the given points has full dimension.
status_evidence.claim: Establishes the conjectured denumerability result on the convergence of Weiszfeld's algorithm.
